text:
support-jane: ACME (tenant acme-inc) reporting large spike in 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference starting ~10:12 UTC. They see p95+ timeouts and a mix of 502/504. Example request_id: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d. Customer says it started after a sustained batch job ramp.

sre-bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway queue_depth(us-west-2) > 95% for 7m. continuous-batcher backlog rising. panels: https://grafana.redwood/boards/queue-depth

ing-ops-rob: grabbing traces now. initial look: KV cache eviction spikes + long seqs from acme causing batcher to stall. Also seeing frequent auth token 401->retry loops from the tenant at the same time.

maria: @support-jane can you get one full trace_id and a minimal repro curl? we need the traceid to follow through the gateway -> batcher -> model worker path.

support-jane: sending logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T10:13:02Z ERROR gateway handler req=req_0a1b2c status=504 queue_wait_ms=12045 batch_size=1 kv_miss=true
2026-03-17T10:13:03Z WARN auth token refresh failed tenant=acme-inc err="temporary backend 503"
2026-03-17T10:13:03Z INFO retrying request req=req_0a1b2d
```

customer-sam: FWIW we did a large batch run from our side at 10:05 UTC (bulk export -> long inputs). We can pause if that helps.

todd: probable chain: tenant longseqs -> frequent KV cache misses -> batcher holds more outstanding tokens per request -> queue depth climbs -> once queue limit hit continuous-batcher starts rejecting with 504 tail timeouts. Auth/billing retries amplify enqueued requests. TL;DR: queue saturation + tail-latency.

eli: immediate mitigation options:
- throttle tenant at gateway for 15m -> rate-limit acme to X rps
- enable fallback routing to smaller model variant (shorter context) for acme
- temporarily increase `batcher.queue_limit` for affected pool (careful: memory spike)

maria: I'll take gateway throttle and fallback. @todd can you prepare a canary rollout to bump `batcher.queue_limit` by 20% in us-west-2 pool? we want measurable effect without full exposure.

todd: on it. Will push canary with deploy-bot. command I will run:
```
kubectl set env deployment/batcher-service -n us-west-2 BATCHER_Q_LIMIT=1200 --record
```
I'll keep it canaryed to 5% of traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy started by todd. canary: batcher-service/us-west-2 -> 5% traffic. change BATCHER_Q_LIMIT=1200.

ing-ops-rob: small note: auth retries are significant. We should ask support to check customer token refresh path; if their refresh backend returns 503 we get retry storms. support-jane please ask acme to check token endpoint.

support-jane: pinged customer: asked to pause large run and check token endpoint. asked for full trace ids and sample request payload (was provided).

maria: we've applied gateway throttle and fallback routing. initial metrics: queue_depth down 30% in 3m, 5xx rate dropping. still seeing occasional tail 504s at p99.

todd: canary shows reduced tail with bumped queue_limit but we saw memory pressure on one worker pod at 10:17. rolling back canary to 2% while we analyze memory footprint of longer contexts.

eli: medium-term: add KV cache prefetch for hot prefixes and tune auth backoff to avoid tight retry loops. Also add a soft limit that reroutes to a lower-cost model variant before hitting hard queue_limit.

maria: action items:
- support-jane: keep customer updated + confirm token endpoint health (ETA 10m)
- todd: capture heap/profile of batcher worker under longseq load (ETA 20m)
- ing-ops-rob: correlate auth retries -> enqueue rate and produce short graph for postmortem (ETA 30m)
- eli: open followup to add prefetch + soft-reroute (RFC)

support-jane: customer paused bulk job and reports immediate reduction in their error surface. they're fine with temporary throttling.

ing-ops-rob: creating incident doc: /incidents/3267894321-queue-shepherding (will add traces + logs). initial root cause hypothesis: tenant longseq burst + KV cache miss storm + auth retry amplification -> queue depth saturation -> continuous-batcher tail timeouts.

customer-sam: thanks team. appreciate the quick mitigation. will follow up on token endpoint and reduce batch sizes.

maria: labeling this incident: severity=high, area=hosted-gateway/batcher, mitigation=throttle+fallback+canary queue limit bump. we'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and then start RCA.

todd: noted memory observation. will attach flamegraph + pod logs to incident doc.

support-jane: closing customer communication loop. will update if they see reoccurrence. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary rollback to 2% completed by todd.

sre-bot: NOTE: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/queue-surge and checklist applied: throttle -> fallback -> canary -> monitor.

maria: leaving this thread open while we collect artifacts. filing postmortem stub now.
